blocks.body:
## Decision

Adopt the process-local WGPU software graph as an explicit low-latency `CapturedCodecDecode` policy, not as the default codec path. It consistently lowers paired device and readback latency and nearly eliminates host graph-construction time, but adds 172 MiB to median observed NVML peak. The ordinary decode path remains the memory-saving default.

## What changed

The session reuses compiled pipelines, bind groups, immediate values, resource transitions, and dispatch order. Per request it performs one bit-preserving GPU-to-GPU latent copy, replays the fixed codec graph, and reads back only final audio. Across five fresh processes, the median paired-block improvement was 0.289 ms at device completion and 0.236 ms through CPU readback. Median host enqueue fell from 0.512 ms to 0.0023 ms.

## Memory trade-off

The dedicated graph arena reserves 176,502,272 additional allocator bytes while retaining only 192,000 additional logical in-use bytes for final audio. Main-pool cleanup did not release its existing reservation. Median NVML peak was 1,358 MiB with the graph session and 1,186 MiB in independent normal-only processes. This is acceptable on the pinned 12 GiB machine for an opt-in latency policy, but it is not a free replacement for the ordinary path.

## Runtime and API contract

`CapturedCodecDecode<'model>` borrows the codec so captured weights cannot be dropped, owns stable input/output buffers, and requires `&mut self` to serialize update and replay. Its safe method returns owned F32 CPU audio; reusable GPU output tensors never escape. Capture rejects synchronization, readback, host writes, profiling, memory-policy mutation, graph nesting, unknown graphs, and cross-stream replay. Dynamic indirect dispatch buffers are retained. Graph destruction synchronizes before releasing its arena.

## Correctness and validation

All graph and normal outputs were bitwise equal with waveform SHA-256 `113ba560546d82a3112332ac67b3cea5d5b83b407109d3df3817e5b82b609e05`; all five paired sessions reported zero uncaptured WGPU errors. Against the independently pinned F16 fixture: max absolute error 0.00341797, RMSE 0.000213971, SNR 56.0742 dB, cosine 0.999998775. Repository validation passed 509 tests with 17 pre-existing manual GPU tests ignored, plus all-target clippy with warnings denied.

## Portability, limitations, and next work

The implementation uses shared WGPU APIs and source and is intended for Vulkan, Metal, DX12, and native WebGPU. Only NVIDIA/Vulkan is measured here; portability is a source-level claim, not a validation claim. Pipelines and graphs are process-local and are not serialized across launches. Each graph is fixed-shape. Next steps are a shape-keyed session cache, Metal/DX12 compile-and-accuracy smoke tests, graph-arena packing to reduce the 172 MiB peak delta, then the fixed-k7 1D halo loader and typed multi-output store transform.

## Reproduction

Use source commit `7159372055f78e037370f9092cc128f38604c2ea`, binary SHA-256 `1d700bff895c9df13311f05266fc53b755227ce9e6537bfef44c6d9ddda162f5`, fixture SHA-256 `08663e52df6c63eea7ebf5ae2ba35778bdb5bc7d20cd06e430e855a86174229e`, and codec SHA-256 `b14a25da5d68bf779d8c44a40706ddc7c4819cb60489b2a80a6408ca03c514fb`. Run five fresh paired sessions with five warmups and ten ABBA/BAAB blocks; sample NVML every 100 ms. Run five separate normal-only fresh processes for VRAM control. Verify the campaign `SHA256SUMS` before aggregation.
